result:
I wrote `/Users/workingmyassof/satbank/spec/v2-upgrades/review.md` (1,588 lines, not committed). It has the four required parts:

- **Scorecard:** 26 of TopTierPrep's features in this area. 9 are already way better in v2. The other 17 were only at parity or below, and each one names the accepted upgrade that fixes it.
- **Accepted upgrades:** 19, V1–V19, each written build-ready with acceptance checks.
- **Spec overrides:** 41 numbered edits inside §3.9. All 73 quoted lines were checked against the spec and each appears exactly once. A second table lists the changes needed outside the section, in Part 2 and in the other upgrade files.
- **Rejected:** about 35 ideas, one line each with the reason.

The biggest upgrades:
- **Due today (V1):** a finite daily list, capped to the student's day and ordered check-ins, relapses, sure-and-wrong, half-fixed, saved, marked, then everything else by points. **Start review · 10 min** replaces "Redo all · 22" as the main button, and the list ends in "Done for today". The nav badge now counts what is left today, not every open mistake.
- **Review my misses (V2):** a walk through test misses. Try it again blind, name the mistake from the question's own wrong-option misconceptions, see the answer, then prove it on a new version of the question.
- **Saved as a spaced deck (V3):** saved questions come back on new numbers at 1, 3, 7 and 21 days, then count as Learned.
- **Points at stake (V4):** every mistake is priced with the Today and Profile points formula, and "Most points" is the default order.
- **Your instincts (V5):** blind spots (sure but wrong), answer changes, and how often flags caught a miss, across every sitting.
- **Fixed that holds (V10):** the Fixed tab separates fixes that have passed a check-in from ones not checked yet, and shows which difficulty each was proven at.
- **See one solved (V11):** a worked example beside the missed question, with the student's own trap marked in it.

The rest cover causes and label corrections, habits, a timeline per mistake, a weekly made-vs-fixed chart, speed, rematches, a faster review pane, options on every list, empty states, Ask for help, paper worksheets whose answers count, and a test-week trap sheet with the student's own rules.

A few things I measured to back the design. 88.6% of misconceptions turn up again within 40 reserved example seeds, so a worked example with the student's trap is cheap. 99% of multiple-choice items carry three named wrong options, so "What happened?" nearly always has three real choices. In the dev database, all 10 closed mistakes closed at the same timestamp they opened, which is why V10 exists.

Two calls you may want to look at:
- **Closing rule unchanged.** I rejected "a mistake closes only on two different days", because `practice.md` already rejected it and the 3-day check-in is the delayed proof. Showing held versus not-checked-yet on the Fixed tab covers the same worry.
- **Reused sibling models.** Every model already defined in the other upgrade files is reused rather than rebuilt. The one real change is that Plan's trap sheet endpoint (L19) now reads from Review's, so both pages print the same list.

No proposal contradicted `v2-decisions.md`. The challenge-sharing rule was reworded to fit the twin daily challenge. New payloads carry a subject field so Reading & Writing can be added later.
